text:
sophia: quick question — when someone clicks "Save query" in the route inspector, should the saved object be bound to the route name, the route id, or to (route id + model version)? I'm worried about silent drift when we do routing rollouts or model variants.

jonah: my vote is route id + model version. if you only bind to route id we can't guarantee the same telemetry/units later. bindings should be deterministic for audits. :thinking:

maya: agree on binding to model version, but UX needs to surface that. most customers expect "saved view" to feel persistent even if backend routing swaps model for perf reasons. we should show a badge: "saved view may be affected by routing" and a link to the currently active model.

ryan: related: quota attribution. If a saved view pins a model version, quota should charge against the active model used to serve requests, not what the saved view stored at creation time. Otherwise cost math gets weird. We should document both behaviors clearly.

jonah: hmm — two behaviors then: (A) "pin" saved query: also pin model in UI and in API and route to pinned model (strong guarantee, counts against pinned capacity). (B) "snapshot" saved query: records the filters/columns and model version for reproducibility but routing still uses normal policy. We can let users choose at save time.

maya: +1 for mode toggle. tiny UX: modal with radio options "Pin model (stable but costs capacity)" vs "Snapshot only (reproducible metadata, routing may change)". default = snapshot. Also show telemetry warning: "if you snapshot, evals/searches might return different results after rollouts".

sophia: what about telemetry/alerts that rely on saved queries? e.g., a regression alert tied to a saved view should track the model actually used for generation. If snapshot-only, alert should annotate which model was used for the evaluation run.

jonah: agree. Implementation sketch for saved-query API object (proposal):
```json
{
  "id": "sq_12345",
  "created_by": "sophia",
  "scope": "route",            // route | org | personal
  "route_id": "r_kittens",
  "route_name": "kittens/short-replies",
  "filters": { ... },
  "model_pin": null,            // null or model id
  "model_snapshot": "redwood/v1.2.0-quant",
  "save_mode": "snapshot",    // snapshot | pin
  "created_at": 1689000000
}
```

maya: that looks good. note: model_snapshot is important for audits. Also add a small boolean `affects_routing` for UI to show badge quickly.

ryan: telemetry tagging: every telemetry emit for saved-query-based runs should include metadata: saved_query_id, save_mode, served_model_id, routing_policy_version. That will let us compute the right attribution and detect regressions when model changes.

engbot: deploy scheduled: prod:routes:save-mode-metadata will run at 2024-11-09T03:00Z; test rollout on staging first.

sophia: next steps: jonah + ryan to draft API contract and backend behavior; maya to design modal and small badge copy; i'll sync with infra to ensure we can surface quota delta in the save modal. thanks all. :thumbsup:

jonah: i'll put a tiny PR with schema changes and a migration plan (add model_snapshot, save_mode, affects_routing) and a compatibility shim for older saved queries. expected work: ~2 days backend + 1 day UX polish.

maya: i'll mock the modal and few states (pin success, insufficient capacity error, snapshot confirmation). will post in #design later today.

ryan: one more: add a telemetry sample rate flag on saved queries for alerts so we can reduce eval cost for high-frequency alerts. small opt-in.

sophia: perfect. leaving this thread as the canonical design decision; we'll reference the PR and the design mocks in the rollout ticket.
